title: Existence and Absence of Spin-Glass Phases on Migdal--Kadanoff Hierarchical Lattices: A Complete Classification
abstract: We consider the Ising spin-glass model on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices, characterized by the fractal dimension $d=1+\log s/\log b$, where $s$ and $b$ denote the number of parallel branches and the number of bonds in series within each branch, respectively. For independent Gaussian couplings, we rigorously establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for arbitrary integers $b,s\ge2$. We prove that a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists whenever \[ \frac{b}{\sqrt{s}} \left( \frac{b\sqrt{s(s-1)}}{bs-1} \right)^{s-1}<1. \] In particular, this condition holds for all three-dimensional MK hierarchical lattices ($d=3$, or equivalently $s=b^2$), regardless of the choice of $b$. Conversely, we prove the absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order for fractal dimensions $d<1+\log17/\log6\approx2.58$, as well as in the large-$b$ limit for any fixed $d<3$. In the intermediate regime $1+\log17/\log6\le d<3$, we provide a finite-step procedure to determine the presence or absence of spin-glass order, which depends on $b$ and $s$. Our results provide a complete characterization of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices.
summary: This work rigorously classifies the existence of finite-temperature spin-glass order on MK hierarchical lattices by analyzing the Renormalization Group flow. It derives a necessary and sufficient condition based on the parameters $s$ and $b$, providing a complete theoretical framework for this class of disordered quantum magnets.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide a complete classification of the existence and absence of finite-temperature spin-glass order on Migdal--Kadanoff (MK) hierarchical lattices.
main_result: It establishes rigorous conditions based on the parameter $\Lambda(b, s)$ to determine if a finite-temperature spin-glass phase exists, providing a complete characterization for arbitrary lattice parameters $b$ and $s$.
method: The analysis relies on exact Renormalization-Group (RG) transformations applied to the Ising spin-glass model, comparing the RG flow parameters at finite and zero temperatures.
model_or_system: The system is the Ising spin-glass model defined on MK hierarchical lattices, characterized by a fractal dimension $d = 1 + \log s / \log b$. The Hamiltonian involves Gaussian random couplings.
key_observables: The spin-glass order parameter, $E[\langle Q_n^2 angle_n]$, is the primary diagnostic tool used to determine the presence or absence of order.
important_parameters: The lattice structure is defined by $s$ (parallel branches) and $b$ (bonds in series). The critical diagnostic parameter is $\Lambda(b, s)$, which dictates the phase transition.
main_assumptions: The analysis primarily assumes independent Gaussian couplings ($J_{ij} \sim N(0, 1)$) and utilizes the exact RG structure afforded by the hierarchical lattice.
paper_structure: The paper develops the RG framework for the spin-glass model, derives the necessary and sufficient condition for order existence based on $\Lambda(b, s)$, and provides specific theorems covering the existence ($\Lambda > 1$) and absence ($\Lambda \le 1$) of the phase.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical techniques used to classify phase transitions in disordered systems, particularly the use of RG flow analysis, are highly relevant to understanding complex many-body physics in quantum materials.
